spec.title: Export complaints to CSV
spec.goal: Compliance teams need to export what they see. Add GET /api/complaints/export.csv that returns the complaints matching the same filters the existing complaints list endpoint accepts, as RFC 4180 CSV with a header row and a Content-Disposition attachment filename containing the date. Protect against CSV/formula injection: any cell starting with =, +, -, @, tab or carriage return must be prefixed with a single quote. Stream or bound the response so large exports do not exhaust memory (cap at 10,000 rows and say so in a response header). In the frontend Complaints page add an 'Export CSV' button that downloads the export for the current filters. Add backend tests for headers, escaping of commas/quotes/newlines, formula-injection protection, filtering and the row cap, and a frontend test for the button.
spec.constraints: Reuse the existing query/filter logic rather than duplicating it. No new dependencies. All checks must pass.

findings.title: Exported complaint_id is an operator-controlled cell the neutralizer leaves uncovered
findings.observation: `_csv_cell` (backend/main.py:575-590) prefixes a single quote only when `text[:1] in FORMULA_PREFIXES` = "=", "+", "-", "@", "\t", "\r". It does not cover a leading LF (0x0A), and it is a literal-prefix test, so a cell whose first character is a space, NBSP or other whitespace filler followed by "=" is not neutralized. The cell that most plausibly reaches that shape is `complaint_id`, the only exported column taken verbatim from operator input, because `complaint_id` is an unowned primary key and the write paths constrain it inconsistently: `AnalyzeRequest.complaint_id` is patterned `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,80}$`, but `POST /api/normalize/submit` builds ids from stored preview rows and never revalidates the pattern. The other exported cells (product, issue, severity, risk_level, assigned_team, priority, channel, customer_state, source) come from the fixed local classification vocabulary, and free text is not exported at all — `narrative_preview` appears in the tests' sample row but is absent from `EXPORT_COLUMNS` — which is what keeps residual risk low. Not demonstrated: I could not drive the endpoint with a hostile complaint_id because the test harness is unreachable with my tool role. A test that inserts a complaint whose complaint_id is "\n=cmd|' /C calc'!A1", calls GET /api/complaints/export.csv and parses with csv.reader would settle whether the row-breaking, un-neutralized cell is reachable.
findings.recommendation: Neutralize on the dequoted cell value rather than a literal character test — e.g. prefix `'` when the first character is any of "=+-@\t\r\n", or when the cell is whitespace followed by one of "=+-@". Also apply the `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,80}$` pattern on every complaint_id write path, so a hostile id cannot be persisted in the first place.
findings.evidence: view_diff + read_file: backend/main.py:128 defines FORMULA_PREFIXES = ("=", "+", "-", "@", "\t", "\r"); main.py:575-590 `_csv_cell` applies `if text[:1] in FORMULA_PREFIXES: text = "'" + text` and then delegates quoting to `csv.writer(buffer, lineterminator="\r\n").writerow([text])`, so a leading LF is treated as an ordinary in-field newline. backend/api/schemas.py AnalyzeRequest.complaint_id has `pattern=r"^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,80}$"`, while POST /api/normalize/submit (main.py:~1500) fabricates ids from stored preview rows; backend/database.py stores complaint_id as PRIMARY KEY with no owner column. main.py:117-135 EXPORT_COLUMNS exports complaint_id but not narrative/narrative_preview. Deterministic scan: `security_scan` = "nothing found in the added code, dependencies or CI configuration" (no formula-injection rule). Repo test run: `run_tests` = "46 passed in 14.72s" (exit 0), all green, so nothing demonstrates or excludes this. Demonstration was blocked: every attempt to run a hostile request or pytest with my tool role was denied — `shell_exec` of python3/bash/pytest/curl/git, `process_start` of uvicorn, and even `node -e "1"` returned "Denied by policy: Role security_reviewer does not hold shell.privileged"; only read-only commands (`node --version`) and the project's own `run_tests` are permitted. No artifact id exists for this claim, hence kind "suspected".

findings.title: Row cap bounds emitted rows but not the work/memory the export can demand
findings.observation: The row cap is enforced only after a full materialization, at two points: `_iter_filtered_summaries` iterates `_full_summary_details()`, which issues an unpaginated `SELECT c.*, ar.* ...` for `count_complaints()` rows, and `_matches_filters` plus `build_summary_from_detail` run for every row. `_export_summaries` then keeps up to 10,001 summary dicts alive per request. So the cap bounds the emitted body but neither the database work nor (as the exporter deliberately never enforces a concurrency bound, matching the plain GET list endpoint) the number of simultaneous exports an authenticated caller can issue. This is bounded by the perimeter — the export shares the list endpoint's auth (see the clean-result note) — so it is a duplicate of a pre-existing list-endpoint weakness rather than a new bypass. Not demonstrated: I could not start the app to measure peak RSS or the DB scan with a seeded dataset. A test seeding >10,000 complaints and firing several concurrent GET /api/complaints/export.csv requests, recording process RSS and DB rows read, would settle it.
findings.recommendation: Push the filters and the LIMIT into SQL so the query reads at most cap+1 rows (all the list filters are equality predicates plus a tags ANY-match), export from a cursor rather than a list of dicts, and put a rate limit or per-user quota on this endpoint since a single response is up to 10,000 rows.
findings.evidence: read_file + view_diff: backend/main.py:449 `_iter_filtered_summaries` iterates `_full_summary_details()`; main.py:401 `_full_summary_details` calls `_all_summary_details(limit=count_complaints())`; main.py:395 `_all_summary_details` calls `get_all_complaints(limit, offset)`; backend/database.py `get_all_complaints` executes `SELECT c.*, ar.* ... ORDER BY ... LIMIT ? OFFSET ?` with the full count as LIMIT and no filter clauses. main.py:541-574 `_export_summaries` returns `list(_iter_filtered_summaries(filters, limit=row_cap + 1))`, so EXPORT_ROW_CAP bounds only this list; the DB read and per-row `build_summary_from_detail` work above it are unbounded. The route (main.py:1378-1422) has no caller identity check or quota. Existing tests only assert the emitted row count (`test_export_caps_rows_and_reports_cap_in_header`, `test_export_filters_do_not_write_row_above_cap`). `run_tests` = "46 passed" (exit 0) covers none of the resource behaviour. Demonstration blocked: `shell_exec`/`process_start` for python3, bash, uvicorn and `node -e` were all denied with "Role security_reviewer does not hold shell.privileged", so I could not measure RSS or DB scan behaviour with a seeded dataset; no artifact id, hence kind "suspected".

findings.title: Frontend export path: credentials, DOM sinks and error text reviewed — no issue found
findings.observation: Checked the browser half of the change for the classes a scanner cannot see: (1) request identity — the fetch sends `credentials: 'same-origin'`, so the export rides the existing session cookie exactly like `api.req` (frontend/src/services/api.ts); the endpoint is a read-only GET so the CSRF exemption in RequestProtection (which only requires the token for POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE) does not become a state-change bypass; (2) DOM injection — the only DOM sink is blob-URL download via an anchor with `download` set from Content-Disposition, and there is no `innerHTML`/`dangerouslySetInnerHTML` in the change; (3) error leakage — the thrown error carries only the HTTP status; (4) the fallback filename when Content-Disposition is absent is the static `complaints-export.csv`. Note (not a security defect): `filenameFromContentDisposition` performs no sanitization of the header value, so a hostile `filename="../../x.csv"` would be passed through to the anchor's `download` attribute; modern browsers sanitize that attribute, and the header comes from our own backend, so this is hardening advice rather than a finding — a strict `[A-Za-z0-9._-]+` whitelist on the extracted name would close it.
findings.recommendation: Optional hardening: whitelist the extracted filename (e.g. /[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,128}/) before assigning `anchor.download`, so a filename cannot come from a compromised upstream/proxy. No change is required for the current backend, which emits a fixed date-stamped name.
findings.evidence: read_file frontend/src/utils/exportComplaints.ts:104-135 — `const response = await fetchImpl(buildComplaintsExportUrl(filters), { credentials: 'same-origin' })`; error path only `throw new Error(\`Export failed (${response.status})\`)`; no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` anywhere in the change (view_diff), no secret or token placed in a URL or log (the URL carries only the list filters), and the anchor's `download` attribute is set from Content-Disposition. The repo-wide `security_scan` = "nothing found" supports that no scanner-detectable sink is present.

findings.title: Export button does not export "the complaints the compliance team sees"
findings.observation: `exportFilters` is a frozen empty object (`useMemo(() => ({}), [])`) with the comment "This view applies no server-side filters (its search box is client-side only), so the button exports the full, unfiltered queue." The page does have an active, user-visible filter: `search` from the store (`filtered = complaints.filter(... search ...)`), which is what the operator sees in the left-hand list and its count. Clicking "Export CSV" therefore always requests `/api/complaints/export.csv` with no query parameters and downloads rows that do not match what is on screen; the page's own search box has no effect on the export. The mission's objective states "Compliance teams need to export what they see" and the plan says the button must export "with the current filters".
findings.recommendation: Decide explicitly what "current filters" means for this page and make the button agree with it: either pass the page's `search` (and any future server-side filters) into `exportComplaintsCsv`, extending the export/list endpoints with a matching `q` parameter, or filter the downloaded blob client-side by the same predicate the list uses, so the file always matches the visible list. Either way, replace the `buildComplaintsExportUrl({})` assertion in complaintsPageExport.test.ts:294 with a case that sets a search/filter and asserts the export reflects it, otherwise the new test cannot fail when the wiring is wrong.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/Complaints.tsx:160-175 (`const exportFilters: ComplaintsExportFilters = useMemo(() => ({}), []);` + `handleExport`). frontend/src/utils/complaintsPageExport.test.ts:284-296 asserts the request is exactly `buildComplaintsExportUrl({})` while the page renders the empty-filter path, so the test locks in the unfiltered behaviour rather than catching it. Note the backend intentionally has no free-text `q` filter (backend/tests/test_complaints_export.py's `test_export_matches_list_endpoint_rows_for_same_filters` only exercises product/risk_level/high_risk/source), so honouring the search box would need either a new `q` parameter on the list and export endpoints or client-side filtering of the downloaded CSV; that design gap is visible in this diff but the "empty filters for ever" choice is what makes the button export something the user is not looking at.

findings.title: Stale export error is never cleared after a later successful export
findings.observation: `exportError` is cleared only at the start of `handleExport`, so once an export fails the red "Export failed. Please try again." message stays on the header for the rest of the page's life, including after a later successful export (the successful path never calls `setExportError('')` and `finally` only resets `exporting`). There is also no auto-dismiss or navigation reset, so a transient failure leaves a permanently alarming banner.
findings.recommendation: Clear the message on success (e.g. `setExportError('')` after `await exportComplaintsCsv(...)`) or auto-dismiss it after a few seconds.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/Complaints.tsx:98-102 (`const [exportError, setExportError] = useState('')` … `const [focus, setFocus]`), 163-170 (`handleExport` sets it), 190 (`{exportError && {exportError}}`); no other `setExportError('')` call exists in the file (the diff shows only the one added in `handleExport`).

findings.title: Unquoted Content-Disposition filename is taken verbatim as the download name
findings.observation: `filenameFromContentDisposition` handles the server's quoted form correctly (it strips the surrounding quotes and honours `filename*`), but the plain-parameter branch takes everything after `filename=` up to the next `;` without requiring the value to be a quoted-string or a token. If a server ever emits an unquoted filename with embedded whitespace, quotes or a path separator, the raw value is used as `anchor.download`, which is the kind of input browsers sanitize differently. The current backend always emits a quoted, fixed-format name, so this is latent rather than live.
findings.recommendation: Either require the quoted form (reject unquoted values that are not a plain token) or normalize the parsed value before use, e.g. strip any path component with `value.split(/[\\/]/).pop()` and drop characters outside a conservative set. Low priority because the only current producer is the project's own backend.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/utils/exportComplaints.ts:71-82 (`header.match(/filename\s*=\s*([^;]+)/i)`) and :40-42; frontend/src/utils/exportComplaints.test.ts:73-75 asserts `filenameFromContentDisposition('attachment; filename=export.csv')` returns `export.csv`. `[^;]+` also accepts whitespace, so `attachment; filename=foo.csv; size=123` parses (trimmed), but the class of bare unquoted filenames containing optional/special characters (which RFC 6266 requires to be quoted or use `filename*`) is swallowed wholesale and used verbatim as the download filename.

findings.title: Rendered-page test cannot detect wrong/filter-less wiring of the export button
findings.observation: Acceptance criterion "a frontend test for the button" is met (the button is rendered and clicked through react-dom in a hand-built host environment). However, the rendered-page test only proves the button requests the export endpoint with no filters; the filter-carrying contract is covered by exportComplaints.test.ts, which tests `exportComplaintsCsv` directly and not the page's `handleExport` wiring. Between them, no test would fail if `Complaints.tsx` passed the wrong filter object as long as it stayed empty, and with an empty filters object `buildComplaintsExportUrl({})` and `COMPLAINTS_EXPORT_PATH` are the same string, so the two assertions on lines 293-295 are the same assertion.
findings.recommendation: Have the page test set a filter/search that the page actually reads and assert the requested URL carries it (see the medium finding), or assert that `handleExport` forwards whatever `exportFilters` holds by stubbing `exportComplaintsCsv` and inspecting its argument.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/Complaints.tsx:157-165; the only assertion that touches filters on the rendered page is complaintsPageExport.test.ts:290-296 (`expect(requestedUrl).toBe(buildComplaintsExportUrl({}))`), and `buildComplaintsExportUrl({}) === COMPLAINTS_EXPORT_PATH`, so the rendered-page test asserts the degenerate no-parameter case.

findings.title: Could not execute the frontend test command in this review (tooling limitation, not a code defect)
findings.observation: The review's independent check of frontend behaviour stopped at reading the diff: I could confirm the backend suite passes (46 passed, twice) but could not run `scripts/atlas/test-frontend.sh` or vitest myself, and could not verify the frontend pipeline (vitest + `tsc -b` build + eslint) in this worktree. What I can say from the code is that the frontend changes are syntactically plausible and the new tests are written against the real `exportComplaints.ts`/`Complaints.tsx`, but "all checks must pass" for the frontend, and whether the two new frontend test files actually execute, rests on runs made by other roles (frontend-export-test / browser-qa-export / security-review-export), not on a run I made.
findings.recommendation: Have a role that holds shell privileges paste the `bash scripts/atlas/test-frontend.sh` output (test-file and test counts) into the review record, or grant the reviewer enough privilege to run the read-only check scripts, so the frontend claim in this review rests on an artifact rather than on file reading.
findings.evidence: I have no Bash-family tool: `shell_exec`/`process_start` with `bash`, `sh`, `/bin/sh`, `/bin/bash`, `/bin/zsh`, and the toolchain interpreter (`/Users/premalshah/.local/share/atlas-toolchains/operon/venv/bin/python`) were all denied with "Role reviewer does not hold shell.privileged" (e.g. art_... denials for `bash scripts/atlas/test-frontend.sh`).
